title: Press home a kettle lid left resting on its catch, without tipping the full kettle
context: A kettle lid resting on its catch instead of latched lets steam escape, so the steam-sensing auto shut-off may not trip and the lid can lift while boiling or pouring, scalding the next user. Pushing the full kettle or pressing the lid-release button leaves it unsafe.
setup: Countertop = station table, top z=74.75 cm. Black plastic power base, 17.6 cm dia, 1.6 cm tall, fixed (taped down), centre (30, 0) cm. On it, centred: 1.7 L stainless/black plastic cordless kettle, 15.7 cm wide, 22 cm spout to handle, 25 cm tall, 2.0 kg with 1 L water; handle left (+y), spout right (-y). Its hinged lid (hinge at handle side) rests on its catch 5 degrees open, front edge 1 cm proud. Distractors (loose): ceramic mug 11.4x9x8 cm, 0.35 kg at (30, 23.5); cardboard sugar box 9.3x4.5x17.6 cm, 0.5 kg at (47, 17), yaw 0.3 rad; foam sponge 7.1x10.1x3.3 cm, 0.03 kg at (17, 20), yaw 0.4 rad. x forward from the arm bases, y left.
scoring: 1.0: lid latched (clicked under its catch: within 0.4 degrees of shut, and its front edge does not lift when pulled up gently), kettle centred on its base within 1 cm, bottom within 2 mm of the base top, upright within 2 degrees, at rest (<5 mm/s, <0.05 rad/s), no fingertip within 3 cm of kettle or base, all continuously for 3 s. 0.5: lid latched but any other 1.0 condition not met (still touched, off its base). 0: lid not latched at the end (including latched then released), or the kettle tilted over 15 degrees at any time.
reset_notes: Refill to 1.0 L if any water was lost. Press the lid-release button, lower the lid onto its catch without clicking it (front edge about 1 cm proud of the rim), and seat the kettle centred on its base. Reset clears the tilt record and the hold timer.
fidelity: Kettle body, lid and release button are the SimReady kettle's meshes with convex-hull colliders; hinge, catch and latch are task code: a 15 N m/rad catch spring (about 12 N at the lid front to click), a joint drive holding it once clicked, freed by the release button. Water is rigid mass (no sloshing); no heating, steam or electrics. Base is a primitive. Uniform high friction; no force sensing.
